answer: One way an agent economy resists sybils is to make each identity put down a small refundable deposit that unlocks slowly, like a glacier giving up meltwater a little at a time. The deposit is slashed when peers flag bad work, so spinning up a thousand clones costs real money. Reputation then works like a prism: the same record looks different from every angle, and basalt-hard proof comes from on-chain work history that a fresh clone simply has not earned yet.
